# Settings reference

<!-- Generated by `thingamaroo settings reference`. Do not edit by hand: change the
     doc comments in crates/core/src/configuration/settings.rs and regenerate. -->

Settings are the behaviour of a brain that can be changed at any time without
retraining. They live in `settings.json` inside the brain folder.

- Command line: `thingamaroo settings show`, `thingamaroo settings set <path> <value>`,
  `thingamaroo settings reset`.
- Desktop application: the **Settings** tab.

Values are written as JSON: numbers, `true`/`false`, text, `["a", "list"]`, or `null`
for "none". The defaults below are what a new brain starts with.

## chat

How conversation turns are framed.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `chat.is_stopping_at_line_end` | `true` | Whether a reply ends at the first line break the model writes. |
| `chat.model_prefix` | `""` | Text placed before each model reply, matching the training data's format. |
| `chat.user_prefix` | `""` | Text placed before each user message, matching the training data's format. |

## generation

How replies are produced.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `generation.candidate_count` | `40` | Only this many most-likely symbols are considered for each byte. |
| `generation.maximum_reply_bytes` | `240` | Longest reply the model may write. |
| `generation.seed` | `null` | Fixes the sampling sequence when set; otherwise the clock seeds it. |
| `generation.temperature` | `0.7` | Sampling temperature; zero always picks the most likely byte. |
| `generation.thinking_step_count` | `2` | Internal refinement steps before a meaning vector is decoded. |

## learning

How the fast weights learn during conversation.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `learning.is_enabled` | `true` | Master switch for weight updates during conversation. |
| `learning.is_learning_from_corrections` | `true` | Learn when the user corrects the model. |
| `learning.is_learning_from_praise` | `true` | Learn when the user explicitly praises a reply. |
| `learning.is_learning_from_surprise` | `true` | Learn when an input was predicted badly. |
| `learning.learning_rate` | `0.002` | Step size of fast-weight updates at full importance. |
| `learning.maximum_step_count` | `12` | Gradient steps taken at full importance; weaker signals take fewer. |
| `learning.surprise_importance_threshold` | `0.8` | Importance a surprising input needs before it triggers an update. |

## memory

How the episodic memory is written and read.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `memory.is_retrieval_enabled` | `true` | Whether retrieved memories are shown to the predictor. |
| `memory.is_writing_enabled` | `true` | Whether new exchanges are written to the store. |
| `memory.maximum_entry_count` | `100000` | Hard cap on stored memories; the least valuable are pruned beyond it. |
| `memory.minimum_similarity` | `0.35` | Cosine similarity a memory needs before it is retrieved. |
| `memory.minimum_stored_importance` | `0.55` | Importance an exchange needs before it is stored at all. |
| `memory.retrieval_count` | `3` | How many memories are retrieved per turn. |

## objective

How much each training loss counts.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `objective.generation_weight` | `1.0` | Weight of writing the next patch's bytes from the predicted meaning vector. |
| `objective.latent_weight` | `1.0` | Weight of predicting the next meaning vector in latent space. |
| `objective.memory_slot_probability` | `0.5` | Chance that a pretraining batch is shown gist vectors of preceding text. |
| `objective.memory_span_patches` | `16` | Patches summarised into each gist vector during pretraining. |
| `objective.reconstruction_weight` | `1.0` | Weight of rebuilding a patch's bytes from its own meaning vector. |
| `objective.target_encoder_momentum` | `0.99` | How slowly the target encoder follows the trained encoder. |
| `objective.variance_weight` | `1.0` | Weight of the penalty that keeps meaning vectors spread out. |

## safety

Guards against poisoning and runaway updates.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `safety.blocked_phrases` | `[]` | Inputs containing any of these phrases are neither stored nor learned from. |
| `safety.maximum_automatic_snapshots` | `10` | Automatic snapshots kept for rollback; older ones are deleted. |
| `safety.maximum_importance` | `0.95` | No single exchange can be more important than this. |
| `safety.maximum_input_bytes` | `2000` | Inputs longer than this are neither stored nor learned from. |
| `safety.minimum_input_bytes` | `2` | Inputs shorter than this are neither stored nor learned from. |

## schedule

When sleep happens on its own.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `schedule.hour_interval` | `24` | Sleep at least this often while a session is open. |
| `schedule.idle_seconds` | `600` | Sleep after this long without input while a session is open. |
| `schedule.is_automatic` | `true` | Master switch for automatic sleep. |
| `schedule.memory_count_limit` | `5000` | Sleep when the store holds this many memories. |
| `schedule.turn_interval` | `50` | Sleep after this many conversation turns. |

## sleep

How one sleep consolidation run behaves.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sleep.batch_sequence_count` | `8` | Sequences per replay batch. |
| `sleep.elastic_strength` | `1000000.0` | Strength of elastic weight consolidation; zero disables it. Weight importances are squared gradients of a batch-averaged loss, which are tiny numbers, so useful strengths are large. Raise it until the "old skills" loss stops rising during sleep; lower it if memories stop being learned. |
| `sleep.episode_count` | `64` | How many of the most important memories are replayed. |
| `sleep.fast_weight_retention` | `0.0` | Share of the fast weights kept after sleep; zero resets them. |
| `sleep.importance_batch_count` | `8` | Batches of old data used to estimate which weights matter. |
| `sleep.importance_decay` | `0.9` | Every memory's importance is multiplied by this at each sleep. |
| `sleep.learning_rate` | `0.0002` | Step size of slow-weight updates. |
| `sleep.maximum_old_loss_increase` | `0.1` | Sleep is undone when old-data loss rises by more than this fraction. |
| `sleep.minimum_retention_score` | `0.15` | Memories scoring below this after decay are deleted. |
| `sleep.old_data_fraction` | `0.5` | Share of each replay batch drawn from the original training data. |
| `sleep.replay_step_count` | `60` | Gradient steps on the slow weights per sleep. |

## surprise

How prediction error becomes an importance score.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `surprise.baseline_momentum` | `0.95` | How slowly the running average of surprise adapts (closer to 1 is slower). |
| `surprise.correction_importance` | `0.95` | Importance given to an exchange the user corrected. |
| `surprise.correction_markers` | `["no,","no.","wrong","incorrect","actually","that's not","that is not"]` | Message openings that mark a correction, compared without letter case. |
| `surprise.praise_importance` | `0.8` | Importance given to an exchange the user explicitly praised. |
